mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC of FEDFUNDS on 20-day returns is less than 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 3.8% triggers a negative market reaction due to heightened recession fears, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises above 3.8%, or the Rank IC of UNRATE on 5-day returns is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC of the interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO growth rate below 0.5% annually), a decline in industrial production signals an impending supply shock that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth rate is below 0.5% annually, or the Rank IC of INDPRO on 20-day returns in that regime is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) above 1600 thousand units signals strong consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above 1600 thousand units, or the Rank IC of HOUST on 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.0% triggers a hawkish monetary policy shift, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 2.0%, or the Rank IC of FEDFUNDS on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a labor market slowdown, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC of the interaction term (PAYEMS * UNRATE) on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) signals an overheating labor market that may trigger a Fed rate hike, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC of PAYEMS on 5-day returns in that regime is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.
